newsitem.title: UK: GBY ruling to boost S. Power profits 15 pct.
newsitem.headline: GBY ruling to boost S. Power profits 15 pct.

text.p: Scottish Power on Monday welcomed the court judgement on Great Britain Yardstick which went in its favour saying it would boost its operating profit by 15 million stg in the 1997/98 financial year.
"The decline in prices will slow. It should increase our operating profits by 15 million stg in 97/98," a Scottish Power spokesman told Reuters.
The spokesman said the court ruling would allow Scottish Power to charge its customers higher rates although the ruling would not alter the current downward trend in prices.
"The downward trend will be slower," he said.
A UK court upheld Scottish Power's claims that a Monopolies and Mergers Commision conclusion on the definition of Great Britain Yardstick should cover its prices.
The Great Britain Yardstick is used in calculating pricing of supply for Scottish companies which have both generation and supply interests.
It is the average price paid by regional electricity companies in England and Wales to buy electricity to supply customers.
Electricity watchdog OFFER had maintained that the MMC decision was only applicable to Scottish Hydro.

"The decision should bring the regulation of the two Scottish companies back into line and reaffirm the link with the England and Wales market prices," Duncan Whyte, Scottish Power's executive director said in a statement.
